methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $75M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Climate & Energy (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Caelux is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Scott Graybeal that has raised $75M to date. The frontier-tech climate sector comprises a limited comp universe of eight private peers and one public comparable (LNZA), including companies such as Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

Valuation analysis is constrained by sparse comparable data at Caelux's stage and valuation tier. The stage-progression method, applying a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression against the $75M raised proxy, yields an implied valuation of $150M. The peer-median approach is not applicable; while eight climate and energy peers exist broadly, zero same-stage, zero adjacent-stage, and zero similar-tier comparables met minimum threshold (≥3 datapoints), making sector-wide median analysis unreliable and potentially misleading.

Given the methodological constraints, the analysis supports a valuation range of $128M to $172M, centered on $150M. This range reflects 15% downside and upside variance around the stage-progression point estimate. Key uncertainties include the limited peer dataset at this valuation tier, the reliance on a single applicable method, and the heterogeneity of climate-tech business models and paths to scale. A follow-on Series B dataset may enable more robust triangulation as the company matures and sector comparables accumulate.
